metaDescription: Six four-burner propane gas grills compared on main-burner BTU, primary grate area, side burner math and build, for families and regular entertainers.
expertTake: The Weber Spirit E-425 is the best four-burner because its boost sear zone, build and long warranty suit a decade of family cooking. The IdeaMaxx 4-burner is the value pick, with about 103 BTU per square inch on a 387 sq in grate. Skip the four-burner class if you cook for fewer than five, because the extra width mostly burns more propane.
introParagraphs: Four burners is the width that suits entertaining. It lets you run two zones for the main course while a third and fourth stay low for sides, buns and resting meat, all on one grate.

Most listings in this class also bundle a side burner into a giant total BTU figure. Reading past that number to the main burners, the primary grate and the build is what separates a real family grill from a bright carton. A little arithmetic on the spec sheet saves a lot of regret on the patio.

products.name: Weber Spirit E-425 4-Burner Propane Gas Grill
products.description:
The E-425 is the four-burner that treats the layout as the feature. Boost burners add about 40 percent more power in a large sear zone, so one end of the grate can run hot while the rest stays moderate. A press-and-turn Snap-Jet igniter lights each burner one-handed.

The design philosophy is heat retention over headline BTU. Heavier castings and a snug lid let the burners cycle less, which is why it can cook better on a lower carton number than the budget grills here. Against the Charbroil Performance it adds the boost zone and a much more solid box.

Weber Works side rails take snap-on tool hooks and a bottle holder, sold separately. In ownership, the grease tray and burners are the wear items, and parts are easy to source. Brush the grates, empty the tray and cover it. It costs the most here, and the premium buys build and parts support, not extra grate. If you rarely cook for more than four, the E-325 does the same job with one fewer burner.
products.bestFor: Families of five or more who want a four-burner that lasts a decade.
pros: Boost burners create a strong sear zone
Snap-Jet ignition lights each burner easily
cons: Lower headline BTU than budget rivals

products.name: IdeaMaxx 4-Burner Propane Gas Grill, 40,000 BTU, 387 sq in
products.description:
The IdeaMaxx puts 40,000 BTU across four independent stainless burners over 387 sq in, about 103 BTU per square inch. That is at the top edge of the useful 80 to 100 band, so it should preheat quickly and sear. Foldable shelves save space when it is stored.

The ratio is the reason it takes the value slot. Many bigger-looking four-burners spread the same fire across more or less area and cook worse. Against the Weber it lacks the boost zone and the warranty, and against the EUHOME it has a slightly lower flux and a simpler layout.

Ownership is simple but not heavy-duty. Expect thinner metal, so cover it and empty the tray often. Parts support is less certain than a major brand. It is the pick for people who want the right physics at a low tier. Foldable shelves also make it easier to tuck against a wall in winter.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want a four-burner with a strong heat-per-inch ratio.
pros: About 103 BTU per sq in preheats and sears quickly
cons: Less certain parts and warranty support

products.name: EUHOME 4-Burner Propane Grill with Side Burner, 46,500 BTU
products.description:
The EUHOME is the clearest example of side burner math. Its 46,500 BTU total includes an 8,500 BTU side burner, so the four main burners deliver about 38,000 BTU. Over the 332.28 sq in primary grate, that is about 114 BTU per square inch, above the useful band.

The listing also gives 458 sq in total, with the primary area being the part you can sear on. Enameled cast iron grates retain and spread heat evenly. The side burner is the practical extra for a pot of sauce or beans.

More flux than you need means more propane for the same steak, so expect to run the burners lower than the knob suggests. Compared with the IdeaMaxx it has a similar grate but a bit more fire and an extra burner on the side. Keep the cast iron oiled and clean the side burner after boil-overs. It suits cooks who want a full outdoor kitchen. The primary grate is the number to trust when planning for guests.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a side burner and enameled cast iron for full outdoor meals.
pros: Separate 8,500 BTU side burner for pots
Enameled cast iron grates retain heat
332 sq in primary grate within 458 sq in total
cons: About 114 BTU per sq in is above the useful band
46,500 BTU headline includes the side burner

products.name: Electactic Stainless Steel 4-Burner Grill with Side Burner
products.description:
The Electactic lists four stainless burners at 8,000 BTU each, so the main burners come to 32,000 BTU, with the remaining 10,000 BTU in the side burner. Its selling point is a stainless body from top to bottom, in contrast to painted steel that chips.

Stainless resists the rust that kills cheaper grills in a few seasons, which matters on a damp patio. A built-in thermometer tracks the lid temperature. Compared with the EUHOME it has a lower main-burner total, so it runs gentler.

The listing's area figures are less clear, so check the primary grate before buying. Clean the stainless with a non-abrasive pad and cover the grill. It is a good choice for humid or coastal climates. Wipe the stainless along the grain to avoid scratches that collect grease.
products.bestFor: Buyers in damp or coastal climates who want a stainless body.
cons: Listing does not clearly state primary grate area
Total BTU includes the side burner

products.name: Nexgrill 4-Burner Propane Grill, 52,000 BTU, 562 sq in

specList.label: Heat flux
specList.value: About 93 BTU/sq in on stated area

products.description:
The Nexgrill has the largest stated area here, 562 sq in, with 52,000 BTU and a side burner. On the stated figures that is about 93 BTU per square inch, which sits in the useful band, though the area likely includes a warming rack. The lid is rust-resistant stainless steel and the grates are matte cast iron.

Cast iron gives even heat and improved release, if oiled. A built-in thermometer and a side burner complete the package. It is a better fit than the IdeaMaxx for hosts who need area, while the IdeaMaxx wins on flux for a small family.

Ownership is typical for this tier: oil the grates, empty the tray, cover it. Expect the painted cabinet to need touch-ups. It suits large cookouts. If you host often, this is the one that gives you room to cook burgers and sides at once.
products.bestFor: Hosts who need the most grate area at a mid tier.
pros: 562 sq in is the largest stated area here
cons: Stated area likely includes a warming rack

products.name: Charbroil Performance Series 4-Burner Cabinet Grill with Side Burner
products.description:
This Charbroil starts as a four-burner gas grill and converts to griddle or charcoal cooking with separate inserts. A side burner covers pots, and a cabinet hides the tank. A 2-year limited warranty backs it.

The warranty tells the story. Two years against Weber's longer coverage means lighter parts, so expect thinner metal and more flare-ups. The conversion options are the attraction: breakfast on a griddle, then charcoal for flavor on weekends.

Store the inserts so they do not rust, keep the tray empty and cover the cabinet. It suits experimenters. It is a fair pick for a family that likes to experiment rather than specialize.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want to switch between gas, griddle and charcoal in one cabinet.
pros: Converts to griddle or charcoal cooking

buyingCriteria.explanation: Side burners inflate the carton figure. The EUHOME lists 46,500 BTU but 8,500 of it is the side burner, and the Electactic lists 42,000 with four 8,000 BTU main burners. Judge the grate on the main burners alone. A buyer who compares carton numbers alone will rank these grills in the wrong order, so always subtract the side burner first.

Divide main-burner BTU by primary grate area and aim for roughly 80 to 100. The IdeaMaxx is near 103, the Nexgrill near 93 on its stated area and the EUHOME near 114. Above 100 mostly burns more propane. The practical test is how quickly the grate reaches 500 F with the lid closed, which a balanced ratio does in about ten minutes.

Totals include warming racks that cannot sear. The EUHOME lists 458 sq in total but 332.28 sq in primary. Allow 70 to 80 sq in per person, and expect a family of five to want 400 sq in or more of primary area. Ask whether the quoted area counts a warming rack, because that is where the padding usually hides.

Four burners give width and a longer cool zone. Burner count is secondary to area and to having enough burners for two zones. Five and six burner grills are mostly about width and side burners, not better cooking. Consider whether you will really use both outer burners, since a three-burner often covers the same cooks.

Heavy castings and a good lid hold heat so burners cycle less. The Weber Spirit E-425 is built around that, while the Charbroil Performance lists a two-year warranty. Build quality matters more than any BTU figure. Read what the warranty covers, since grates and finishes are often limited to a shorter period than burners and the cookbox.

Painted steel chips and rusts, while stainless resists weather. The Electactic is stainless throughout, and the Nexgrill has a stainless lid. In humid climates this decides lifespan. A grill kept under a cover in a dry place will outlast one left bare in rain, whatever its material.

howWeEvaluated.title: Main-burner heat
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated side burner BTU from main-burner BTU. The EUHOME and Electactic listings made that possible, and we flagged totals that blur it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heat per square inch
howWeEvaluated.description: We divided main-burner BTU by primary area where stated. The IdeaMaxx near 103 and the Nexgrill near 93 sit near the band, and the EUHOME near 114 sits above it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Warranty and build
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared warranty and body material. The Weber's build led, the Charbroil Performance lists two years, and the Electactic earned credit for stainless.

howWeEvaluated.title: Usable grate
howWeEvaluated.description: We applied 70 to 80 sq in per person. The Nexgrill's 562 sq in and IdeaMaxx's 387 sq in cover large and mid families. We also treated grate area beyond what a household needs as a cost, not a benefit, since a big chamber burns more fuel on small cooks.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on owner feedback patterns, we weighed igniter wear, burner corrosion and paint chipping. Parts support counted. We also noted that a grill with an available replacement-burner part is a better long-term buy than one without.

howToChoose.subheading: Side Burner versus No Side Burner

cards.label: Side burner
cards.text: EUHOME, Electactic, Nexgrill and Charbroil add a side burner for sauces and sides. It inflates the total BTU figure.

cards.label: No side burner
cards.text: The Weber Spirit E-425 and IdeaMaxx skip it and spend on the grate and sear zone.

howToChoose.note: Pick a side burner if you cook full meals outside. Skip it to put the money into the grate. A side burner is also the one feature that makes a grill feel like an outdoor kitchen, so weigh that against pure grate quality.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for 400 sq in or more of primary grate and a side burner. Width matters more than raw BTU.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Nexgrill has the most stated area, and the EUHOME and Nexgrill both add side burners.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You grill weekly for years. The Weber Spirit E-425 earns its tier with build and a sear zone.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You entertain occasionally. The IdeaMaxx gives the right ratio at a low tier.

maintenance.why: Burnt residue creates off flavors and attracts rust. A hot brush right after cooking takes about a minute and keeps enamel and cast iron in good shape. Use a nylon brush on porcelain or enamel to avoid chipping.
Grease buildup is the main cause of flare-ups and grease fires. Empty it before it fills, and line it with foil if the manual allows.
Brush soapy water over the hose and fittings with the gas on. Bubbles mean a leak and a part to replace.
Spider webs and debris block ports and cause uneven flames. Clear them with a straightened paper clip or a venturi brush.
Boil-overs clog the side burner and cause weak flames. Wipe it after it cools and clear the ports.

faq.a: For five or more people or regular entertaining, yes. Four burners give two cook zones and room for sides. For a couple, a two-burner uses less propane. Many households cook happily on three, so count your usual guests before paying for width you will not fill.

faq.q: Does a side burner count in the BTU figure?
faq.a: Usually yes. The EUHOME lists 46,500 BTU but 8,500 of it is the side burner. Judge the grate on the main burners alone. That is why two grills with the same carton number can cook very differently.

No. About 80 to 100 BTU per square inch of primary grate is the useful band. More than that mostly burns extra propane. A grill with a thick lid and a sensible ratio will out-cook a thin box with a bigger number on the carton.

faq.q: How long does a four-burner last?
faq.a: A Weber can last ten years or more. Unbranded models last four to six with care. Warranty length is a rough guide. Covering the grill and cleaning the grease tray extend the life of any of them by years.

faq.q: Can I use propane on a balcony?
faq.a: Often not. Propane is the most restricted fuel, and rules depend on fire code, your lease and the unit's listing. In some cities even storing a standard propane barbecue on a balcony is illegal, so check all three before buying.
Clean the tray, brush the grates and trim fat. Thin metal cools unevenly and lets grease pool. Preheating with the lid closed and keeping burner ports clear also helps the flames stay blue and even.
